items.title: Michi Fuji interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014
items.q: But this trio, Junior is great at accompanying and the rhythm is real. And Hide is very great. This trio is fine.

ctx.x: Do you like working without a drummer or does it not matter to you?

I love drummers and I need to feel more drum feeling. But this trio, Junior is great at accompanying and the rhythm is real. And Hide is very great. This trio is fine. But © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -7-
always I’m learning a lot of things from a drummer. Because the violin is hard to feel and play with a rhythm feel.

items.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014
items.q: And his student, Michi, anyway, always sometime he wanted to use a violin player.

ctx.x: Yeah there’s actually a couple of jokes about that. How to get people to talk? Take a bass solo. That’s very neat. I noticed last night when you were playing that when it was time for your solo that you did something different to stand out. Whether it was with a bow or going up high. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-

Actually this trio is kind of different. And Junior really wanted to play talking together sometimes. Not this is a piano solo. Not this is a bass solo. But he wanted to play sometimes all together. Sometimes speak all together. You know he plays something, even if this is his solo, but I play something — that’s why he made this trio. So he said this was the first experience of this kind. It’s just happened after he started hiring me and we kind of developed a duo, just a duo, minus the drums, just a duo. Duo…
